member.name: M:SolidCore.Coroutines.CoroutineRunner.RunToCompletion(System.Single,System.Int32)
member.summary:
Headless drain: ticks as fast as the CPU allows — advancing simulated time by per tick — until all coroutines finish or is hit; returns ticks executed. Starts are immediate — no flush needed.
This does not wait in real time: a WaitForSeconds(2) completes in microseconds (~120 back-to-back ticks). Use it for tests/batch simulation. For wall-clock waiting, use ; in a game loop, call once per frame instead.

member.name: M:SolidCore.Coroutines.CoroutineRunner.RunRealtime(System.Single,System.Single)
member.summary:
Real-time pump: advances the scheduler in fixed steps paced by actual wall-clock time (via ), so WaitForSeconds(2) blocks ~2 real seconds. Sleeps between polls rather than busy-spinning, and runs until all coroutines finish or elapses (0 = no timeout). Returns fixed steps executed.
Blocks the calling thread. In a game loop, call once per frame instead.

member.name: T:SolidCore.Coroutines.CoroutineCallbacks
member.summary: Process-wide side table mapping the stored in a blittable instruction back to a managed delegate. Instructions live in native BurstArray memory and therefore cannot hold delegate references directly; this registry is the indirection that lets and accept ordinary managed callbacks — the form Unity's IL2CPP/Mono runtime supports (unmanaged function pointers are not usable there).
member.remarks:
Predicates and actions occupy independent 1-based id spaces; id 0 means "no callback". The resolving already knows the instruction , so it selects the correct space without the id encoding it.
Registration happens at authoring time and resolution happens during a tick — which, under , runs on worker threads while authoring may still be appending on another thread. Both paths are guarded by a single lock: correct, and cheap for the primary single-threaded path where callbacks are far rarer than . If the multi-threaded callback path ever becomes hot, switch the read path to a copy-on-write snapshot for lock-free resolution.
The table is append-only and never shrinks; delegates registered from authoring-time templates live for the process lifetime.
